q: What is narrowing?
a: Checking a value (typeof, ===, in, Array.isArray, instanceof, if (x)) so TypeScript knows a more exact type inside that branch.

q: any vs unknown: what is the difference? Which do you prefer?
a: any switches TypeScript off (you can do anything, even wrong things). unknown forces you to check the value before using it. Prefer unknown.

q: Why is `value as Product` dangerous?
a: It only tells TypeScript to trust you. Nothing is checked, not at compile time and not at runtime. If the data is different, you crash later.

q: What does the ! in `user!.name` do, and what can go wrong?
a: It removes null/undefined from the type without any check. If user really is undefined: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined.

q: Why do many teams prefer `'passed' | 'failed'` over `enum Status`?
a: Unions are plain strings (match API JSON directly), create no runtime code, need no import to use the values, and have no numeric-enum surprises.

q: Error: "Type '"superadmin"' is not assignable to type 'Role'." Fix?
a: 'superadmin' is not one of the values in the Role union. Use an allowed value (Ctrl+Space shows them) or add it to the union.

q: Error: "Property 'data' does not exist on type 'Result'." Why?
a: Only one member of the union has data. Check the discriminant first: if (result.ok) { result.data }.

q: Error: "'text' is possibly 'null'." What are your options?
a: if (text !== null) { ... }, text ?? 'default', or text?.method(). Avoid text! unless you are 100% sure.

q: Which Playwright methods return string | null?
a: locator.textContent() and locator.getAttribute(name) (both after await). Handle the null case.
